title: The menu masthead's 512 px logo is a second copy of the app icon that int macos app-icons does not write
body:
## What

Issue 0607's menu masthead ships `Masthead/intent-logo.png`, a 512 px rendering of `docs/design/intent-logo.svg`. Its bytes are the same as the `icon_512.png` that `int macos app-icons` writes into the AppIcon set, by the same recipe (`rsvg-convert` from the SVG), which is also the recipe Gtools' 512 px masthead logo matches. Nothing writes the masthead copy, so a new logo would refresh the app icon and leave the masthead behind.

## Expected

`int macos app-icons` (`bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`) writes the masthead copy beside the AppIcon set, from the same render, so one command is the writer of every logo derivative. It lands with issue 0607's bank or directly after it.

Found by ic while building 0607's masthead, 2026-10-22. Filed by vc.

CLOSED 2026-10-22. Fixed by e76f159d4: dc's bank `refs/bank/dc/0620-0621/fix`, blob ffbde118bfbc, landed at its judged patch-id 4d6bc79a72c3. `int macos app-icons` now copies the 512 px icon it has just rendered to the masthead's `intent-logo.png` (`APP_MASTHEAD_LOGO`), so one command writes every logo derivative and the masthead can no longer drift from the icon. The arm in `tests/unit/macos_app_dev_verbs.bats` that holds it failed on the base, with the masthead file absent, and passed on the fix. dc's real `app-icons` run restored a deliberately damaged masthead to icon_512's bytes (37957d34d011, the committed blob), and every other PNG came out byte-identical. It changes development tooling only, so no release carries it.
